sentence: This project builds magnetic resonance nanoprobes and a subtraction imaging method to detect early brain metastases in patients with cancer.
This project tests whether combining immune checkpoint modulators, delivered through an oncolytic virus, can improve therapy in mouse models that resist immunotherapy.
This project studies how adult stem cells in flies unevenly pass on histones when they divide, looking at chromatin and DNA replication timing.
This project develops a therapy using regulatory T cells with a chimeric antigen receptor to fight ischemia reperfusion injury in deceased organ transplants.
This project tries to find out how a nuclease protein helps repair broken DNA in cancer cells that are deficient in homologous recombination.
This project develops an AI-driven tool using health records and neighborhood data to help identify women who could benefit from pre-exposure prophylaxis.
This project tests whether a cell culture platform using a patient's own cells predicts which therapies work in metastatic prostate cancer.
This project uses genetically modified T cell therapy and gene editing to target cancer-specific antigens in hematologic malignancies.
This project studies how a signaling axis with elevated oncogenic proteins drives melanoma and whether targeting it could improve treatment.
This project tries to find out how inflammatory mediators from T cells and forebrain circuits link asthma to fear dysregulation.
This project studies how household income, race and insurance affect the use of continuous glucose monitoring in children with type 1 diabetes.
This project tries to find out why proteasomal inhibitors used against blood cancer cause cardiovascular toxicity, using tissue engineering and genome-wide screening.
This project studies how early experience after birth shapes wiring in the mouse visual cortex, using transcriptomics, epigenomics and connectomics.
This project studies how a protein that marks heterochromatin helps keep 3D genome structure in Acute Myeloid Leukemia cells.
This project develops and tests imaging methods for alpha-particle emitters to support dosimetry and treatment planning for patients.
This project uses organic synthesis, mass spectrometry and public data mining to identify small molecules in the human body.
This project develops a product for controlling Aedes aegypti mosquitoes and tests it in semi-field trials and small-scale open-air pilots.
This project studies whether molecules called eicosanoids link persistent inflammation from HIV infection to heart disease in people with HIV.
This project tries to find out how checkpoint blockade immunotherapy may switch on immunosuppressive mechanisms that help tumors grow.
This project studies how fleas defend themselves from infection under natural conditions.
